title: Chip-firing on the quadrant: the bottom-triangle conjecture checked to 2^34 chips
statement: For chip-firing on the directed quadrant Z_{>=0}^2 from N chips at the origin (Inagaki-Khovanova-Luo, arXiv:2601.09125), the bottom triangle of the passing-chip array F (maximal final run of antidiagonal rows whose numbers of nonzero entries drop by exactly 1 per row) has exactly (longest row length) - 1 rows for N = 2^n, n <= 34 (their Conjecture 7.3, previously checked for n <= 12), and for every N with 2 <= N <= 300000. Proved: once a row of F is thin (k-th entry from the nearer end at most 2k + 1), every later row is thin and one entry shorter; the conjecture would follow from the observed statement that the first thin row is a longest row entered by a length increase and the last row has length 2.
resolves: nothing; extends the evidence for IKL Conjecture 7.3 from n <= 12 to n <= 34 and to all chip counts N <= 300000
verified: check_quadrant.py: calibration with IKL (92 rows at n = 9, T(10) = 38570, longest row 13 at n = 9); Conjecture 7.3 for n <= 18 and for all N <= 3000; the thin-row lemma on 20000 random thin rows and on every thin row of F for N <= 3000, with a control showing its no-zero hypothesis is needed; the structure (S) for N <= 3000 (pure Python).

quadscan.c: exact uint64 row recursion for N = 2^n, n <= 34, and every N <= 300000, checking the conjecture, IKL Prop 6.2 (lengths change by exactly 1), the absence of interior zeros and (S); zero failures (evidence/quadrant_scans.json).

CALIBRATION gate: the n = 9 array reproduces all four summands of IKL Example 5's partition, 10 + 13 + 57 + 12 = 92 (top triangle, middle top, rectangle, bottom triangle), the rectangle's 57 rows alternating 12 and 13 and starting with 12 included. The apparent discrepancy recorded before 0.1.2 -- our maximal alternating stretch has 59 rows -- is a boundary convention and not a disagreement: the bottom triangle begins at the last longest row, so its first two rows are also the last two of the alternating stretch, making the rectangle exactly two rows shorter. Verified for 6 <= n <= 16 that the bottom triangle starts at the last longest row and that the alternating stretch has the short length at both ends.
unresolved: a proof of Conjecture 7.3 or of (S)
nonclaims: no proof of the conjecture is claimed
the reading of 'number of rows in the bottom triangle' as the maximal final run of length drops by 1 is ours; it reproduces the paper's n = 9 description
smallest_decisive_test: An N = 2^n whose final run of rows with unit length drops has a size different from (longest row length) - 1.
